evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.77.3: nec sē impūne lātūrum putāret, escape unpunished (Lewis & Short s.v. impūnis)
terms.comment: “Get off scot-free” is impūne ferre (Lewis & Short); the adjective impūnis is very rare, the adverb frequent and classical.

evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.5.149: injūriam inultam impūnītamque dīmittere (Lewis & Short s.v. impūnītus)

sources: Lewis & Short: impunis · Lewis & Short: impunitus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 196, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
